outcome: Postoperative complications (fever, pain, menstrual volume decrease)
cohort: The cohort consisted of eighty patients diagnosed with Cesarean Scar Pregnancy (CSP) who received treatment at the study hospital.
finding: Abdominal aortic balloon occlusion resulted in lower radiation exposure for both the operator and patient compared to uterine artery embolization in patients with cesarean scar pregnancy, and both methods effectively reduced bleeding during uterine curettage.
